title: Exclusive / Conservative AI safety group proposes export controls, visa restrictions
key_facts: Humans First, a conservative-led group advocating stronger AI guardrails, released an 'America First AI Policy' platform on Friday 16 Oct 2026, according to a memo shared first with Semafor.
It calls for tighter export controls against China and other adversaries, mandatory independent testing for large AI companies, and a ban on advanced practices such as recursive self-improvement.

It also calls for a ban on federal use of cameras like Flock, public reporting of AI incidents, liability for frontier AI developers for reckless conduct, strict rules for AI used by children, and a pause on H-1B visas.
Russ Walker, the group's executive director and an adviser to Donald Trump's 2020 campaign, said it is time for Congress and conservatives in particular to lead on the issue.
The group is chaired by Amy Kremer, a longtime Tea Party activist who is leading a bus tour called the 'AI Data Center Revolt'.
Semafor says the priorities go beyond what some Republicans interested in regulating AI have proposed and significantly beyond the Trump administration's current light touch.
Semafor adds the group may have more sway if Republicans do poorly in the midterms and AI anxiety is a factor.
